That's it — now start sessions from the **Claude mobile app** and they can reach this dataset. (Prefer an allowlist over "Full"? Choose **Custom** and add `huggingface.co` and `*.hf.co`.) Cloud sessions require a Pro, Max, or Team plan.
Then, in a Claude Code session, paste one line and ask a question:

```
Use the HuggingFace dataset Drbellamy/icml-2026 (config "papers", it's parquet).
Build me a personalized ICML Wednesday schedule — I care about RL infra,
agents, and efficient inference. Give me titles, times, and rooms.

```

The agent loads the parquet, filters, and hands you a plan.
##   ⟨59⟩ Schema — `papers` config (one row per paper)   
| column  | type  | description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| `track`  | string  |  `main_conference` or `workshop`  |  
| `paper_type`  | string  |  `oral`, `spotlight`, `poster`, or `workshop`  |  
| `title`  | string  | paper title  |  
| `authors`  | list[string]  | author names in order  |  
| `abstract`  | string  | full abstract  |  
| `day`  | string  |  `tuesday` … `saturday` (Seoul time)  |  
| `date`  | string  | ISO date, e.g. `2026-07-07`  |  
| `session`  | string  | session / workshop name  |  
| `session_start_kst`  | string  | ISO 8601, Asia/Seoul  |  
| `session_end_kst`  | string  | ISO 8601, Asia/Seoul  |  
| `location`  | string  | room / poster board  |  
| `workshop`  | string  | workshop name (null for main track)  |  
| `url`  | string  | ICML page  |  
| `pdf`  | string  | PDF link (OpenReview) where available  |  
| `openreview`  | string  | OpenReview forum link where available  |  
**Other configs:** `main_conference_full` (all 6,341 accepted main-track papers with PDFs, author IDs, keywords, and spotlight/regular tier), `events` (180 tutorials / invited talks / expo / socials, with abstracts and speaker bios), `workshops` (44 workshops with organizers and summaries). Per-day JSON is also in `by_day/`⟨67⟩ for people who want structure over tables.
##   ⟨60⟩ Example questions to ask an agent 
  * _"Find every**oral** paper mentioning **diffusion** and list its time and room."_
  * _"Build my**Tuesday** : I care about **RL** and **robotics**. No overlaps."_
  * _"Which**authors** have the most papers at ICML 2026?"_
  * _"List all**workshop papers on interpretability** with their PDF links."_
  * _"Cluster**Wednesday's poster abstracts** into themes and summarize each."_
  * _"What are the most common**keywords** among **spotlight** papers?"_


##   ⟨61⟩ Recipes 
**Schedule builder** — _"Given I care about X and Y, plan each day with no time conflicts; output a table of title / time / room / type."_ **Topic discovery** — _"Embed the abstracts and cluster into 15 topics; name each and count papers."_ **Reading list** — _"Rank all posters by relevance to 'long-context efficiency' and give me the top 25 with PDF links."_ **Social graph** — _"Who are the most prolific authors, and which pairs co-author most often?"_
##   ⟨62⟩ Reproduce it / scrape your own conference 
The full pipeline is open-source: **github.com/DavidBellamy/icml2026-scraper⟨68⟩**. Any conference's virtual site + OpenReview + an agent = a queryable conference in your pocket.
##   ⟨63⟩ Coverage & provenance 
  * **Source:** the official ICML 2026 virtual site (`icml.cc/virtual/2026`) and OpenReview, July 2026.
  * **Papers with PDF/OpenReview link:** 9,801 / 10,815. The rest are papers whose titles didn't cleanly match across sources, plus workshop **invited talks** (no paper/PDF exists).
  * **Times** are in **Asia/Seoul (KST)** , the conference timezone. The `main_conference_full` config also carries UTC where relevant.
  * **1 workshop** ("Game Theory in Nature") had not published its schedule at scrape time, so its papers are absent.
  * This is a community scrape, refreshed during the conference. Counts may shift slightly as organizers finalize schedules.
